gaps.note: The data sheet lists Rack Mount Kit 590003, DIN Rail 590012 and Rack Mount Tray 590033. The quick start describes 590003 as a tab with two rack screws, two nuts and three screws, fixed to the side. No held document dimensions any of them, so none is modelled.
gaps.wanted: The kit installation guide for 590003, 590012 and 590033.

gaps.note: The front prints eight lamps, the two lamps of the RJ45 jack and three marks along the SFP cage. The rear shows a light pipe at the corners of each switch jack. No held document gives the colours or meanings, so each placed lamp is drawn off. The photograph shows the RJ45 jack lamps green, sampled #2d5b36 over 56 px. It shows the three SFP marks red, sampled #d12d32 over 15 px for the middle one. The eight other front lamps are dark. The four signal lamps and the three SFP marks are small rectangles in the photograph. They are drawn as the library's round lamp, a stand-in for the shape.
gaps.wanted: A hardware guide with the LED table.

cellular.note: Data sheet: ACM7004-5-L has a 4G LTE modem (Sierra Wireless EM7565, Cat-12) and two SIM card slots. Quick start, page 3: slide the carrier mini SIM into the slot with the contacts facing up. The rear photograph labels the antenna jacks (M), a satellite symbol and (A). The jacks are SMA by the registry's reading of the photograph. No document names the connector, which is recorded in the gaps.

chassis.note: Data sheet, Dimensions and Weight: 5 1/8 x 4 3/4 x 1 3/8 in, 13 x 12 x 3.5 cm, 0.6 kg. Form factor "Compact". The user manual's appendix prints the same 13 x 12 x 3.5 cm. The rack kit 590003 and the DIN rail kit 590012 are accessories and no source dimensions them, so the body is drawn alone.

front-layout.note: Method: the ACM7004-5-L front photograph of the Quick Start Guide is measured against the 130 mm data sheet width. It is 717 px wide, straight on, with no scale marker, so 5.5 px/mm across. Every position on the front is read off the photograph, good to about 0.7 mm. These are the SFP cage, the RJ45 jack, the lamps and their symbols, the two SIM slots and the printing. The lamps, slots and printing right of the network ports are the ACM7004-2-L's to within 1 mm.

lamps.note: The front photograph shows four lamps at the left. A power symbol, a heartbeat symbol, IOIO and an antenna symbol sit beside them. Four signal lamps sit at the right of the SIM slots beside a signal-bar symbol, all dark. Three small red marks sit along the top of the SFP cage at 4.5 mm pitch. They are sampled #c23639, #d12d32 and #d83b35 over 11, 15 and 17 px. They are drawn with the library's round lamp, larger than the marks and round where the marks are small rectangles. The rear photograph shows a small light pipe at each corner of each switch jack. No document held gives a colour or a meaning for any of them, so each is drawn off and states are a gap.

livery.note: The red and black front, the two diagonal stripes, the wordmark and the printing are read off the front photograph. They are painted livery, not parts. The red is the photograph's sampled median, #fa0024 over 800 px. The logo mark is a simplified outline.

network.note: Data sheet: ACM7004-5 has 4 x 10/100/1000 Ethernet switch ports and 1 x 10/100/1000 Ethernet/SFP uplink, all with 1500 V AC isolation. The front photograph prints NET1(S) over an SFP cage and NET1(C) over an RJ45 jack. They are one combo port, drawn as two placements sharing the number. The rear photograph prints NET2 and the numbers 1 to 4 round the switch block. The quick start footnote says NET2 is the built-in switch. ACM700x-2 Quick Start Guide, page 1, step 03: NET1 connects to the primary network. That guide covers the -2 units. NET1 of this model is read the same way, so both halves of the combo uplink are traffic ports.

power.note: Data sheet: 110-240 V AC to 12 V DC external power adapter, consumption less than 11.5 W. ACM700x-2 Quick Start Guide, page 1, kit table: the 12V switching DC power supply in the box is part 450031. Data sheet optional supplies are 450037, 450039 and 450041. The rear prints 9~30V DC under a four-position housing, with a line over five dashes. The user manual's appendix says less than 30 W for all models. The data sheet's 11.5 W is followed. The appendix gives 5 to 50 C ambient where the data sheet gives -25 to 60 C. The data sheet is followed.

rear-layout.note: Method: the ACM7004-5-L rear photograph of the Quick Start Guide is 1127 px wide. The body is 1075 px across for 130 mm (8.27 px/mm), so the face is orthographic to about 1 percent. The two RJ45 blocks, the SMA jacks, the USB ports and the power housing are read off it, good to about 0.5 mm.

serial.note: Data sheet: ACM7004-5 has 4 RJ45 RS-232 "Cisco straight" pinout console ports, 50 to 230,400 bps, and a 4 port embedded gigabit switch. The photograph numbers the serial ports 1 and 2 on the left and 3 and 4 on the right. It prints SERIAL beneath.

serial-role.note: The serial ports are console server ports. ACM700x-2 Quick Start Guide, page 3, "Configure managed devices": set the Console Server Mode radio button for a port. The data sheet calls them "console ports".

sides.note: The outlines are drawn from the data sheet's stated size. The data sheet photograph of the ACM7004-2-L shows the top lid at an angle as a plain dark slab, with no detail to place. No held picture shows the bottom or either side. The user manual says the connection status can be seen from the LEDs on top of the device.

sources.note: Opengear Resilience Gateway ACM7000 data sheet (October 02, 2026): console specifications, interfaces, power, dimensions, weight, model table, package checklist and accessories. Resilience Gateway Quick Start Guide for the ACM7004-2-L, ACM7008-2-L and ACM7004-5-L (06052019), page 2: the front and rear photographs with callouts. Its footnote says NET2 is the built-in switch on the ACM7004-5 units.

usb.note: Data sheet: 4 x USB 2.0 console ports. The rear photograph shows two stacked pairs of USB-A jacks, lettered A and B on the left and C and D on the right. The user manual, section 3.1.8, puts the ACM7008-2 USB ports on the front. The photograph puts them on the rear, and the drawing follows the photograph.
